subject: assets/road/runtime_fullwidth_100m_rough_marked_2mm_20cm_heightmap_v1
verdict: All three runs meet every acceptance gate. The audit still reports not-passed, solely on camera/encoder geometry alerts, all of which occur at pass starts with zero contact sliding.
online_and_offline_detectors_agree: The plugin's online alert count and the offline audit's independently produced 4, 4 and 5 for the three runs. That was the main implementation risk when the trigger was added and it is closed.

geometry_alerts.all_at_pass_starts: mean speed over the alerting intervals is 0.58 m/s against a 2.78 m/s cruise
geometry_alerts.the_two_inside_roi_are_marginal: x = 0.31 and 0.28 m, just past the entry
geometry_alerts.contact_tangential_speed_mm_s: NOT MEASURED: probe_contact_kinematics was false; see retraction_2026_09_16
geometry_alerts.reading: The body tracks the encoder to within 2.72 mm while the camera optical centre lags by 13.6 to 31.8 mm. Body pitch changes by at most 3 mrad over these intervals and accounts for under 3.2 mm of that with the camera's 1.0416 m lever. Mount flex and contact sliding were both unmeasured, so the cause is not established.

pitch_hypothesis_outcome.pre_registered_test: transfers if every alert is in an acceleration or recovery phase AND the residual after the height*pitch estimate stays below 1 mm
pitch_hypothesis_outcome.phase_condition: met: all thirteen are at pass starts
pitch_hypothesis_outcome.residual_condition: not met: 4 of 13 exceed 1 mm, maximum 1.79 mm
pitch_hypothesis_outcome.why_that_verdict_is_less_informative_tha: The hypothesis was formulated against a 12.14-12.38 mm encoder-minus-body gap seen on the 3 mm road. On this road encoder-minus-body is at most 2.72 mm, so there is almost no body-level deficit left for a pitch term to explain and the residual is noise around a small number. The criterion was testing the wrong quantity for this surface; the 13-32 mm gap that does exist is camera-versus-body and the pitch estimate does not address it.
pitch_hypothesis_outcome.what_is_settled_regardless: nothing about sliding: the contact velocity evidence was never collected

limitations: The instance was not freshly restarted; uptime went from 7h58m to 8h27m across the series and RTF is compared within the series, not against section 6 fresh-instance figures.
Three runs establish a range, not a rate.

Run 1 needed three attempts: a broker chassis-HOLD prepare race, then a fault I introduced by publishing the new alert on /linescan/status, which agv_mission/capture.py turns into CAMERA_<reason>. Neither reached capture on the road. The prepare retry was added mid-series, so all three runs carry it but run 1 was its first exercise.

The alert event records the interval's line numbers but not its timestamps, so locating it inside the flight dump required integrating wheel speed backwards to the encoder distance. Adding the timestamps was deliberately deferred so runs 2 and 3 stayed identical to run 1.
Each geometry dump is 7.2 MB now that contact points carry velocities; thirteen dumps across three runs, with no measurable RTF cost.
not_closed: the 0.5 to 4.9 mm left after the pitch term, with mount flex unmeasured
the 13-32 mm gap between body travel and the recorded scan-line ground position during pass-start acceleration
whether the geometry floor of 0.95, set on a flat road whose minimum was 0.9910, is the right rule for a surface that pitches
the pitch explanation remains testable only on the 3 mm scene, where the body-level gap it was built for actually appears

what_was_withdrawn: 'contact tangential speed is 0.0000 mm/s in all thirteen intervals, so there is no tyre sliding'
'the discrepancy is between the vehicle and the recorded ground position of the scan line, an imaging chain projection or timing question'
retraction_2026_09_16.why: All three runs had probe_contact_kinematics false. gz_linescan.cpp:134 gates contact point velocity (691), camera pose (591) and mount joint angles (597) behind that flag, and every dump records probe_contact_kinematics false, camera_pose_available false, velocity_available false on 0 of 9256 contact points, and camera_xyz [0,0,0]. The zeros were uninitialised defaults. My reduction wrote max([...]+[0]) over an empty list, turning absence of evidence into a measurement of zero -- the exact failure ContactTangentVelocity guards against with nullopt and 'absence of evidence must not become zero slip', and that summarize_startup_contact.py asserts against with 'contact velocity evidence incomplete'. I wrote a reduction without that assertion.
retraction_2026_09_16.second_error: camera_position_world_m is the camera optical centre, z = 1.0416 m, not a scan-line ground intersection. The camera rides about 1.04 m up on a pitching body through a flexible mount, so extra horizontal motion of that point is expected and is not by itself evidence of a projection or timing fault.
what_still_stands: every acceptance gate in all three runs, which comes from results.json and the audit's integrity half and does not depend on the probe flag
13 alerts, 4/4/5, all at pass starts, 11 outside the ROI and 2 just past the entry
online and offline detectors agreeing at 4, 4 and 5
encoder minus body of -1.81 to 2.72 mm: body pose and wheel speed are recorded unconditionally
encoder minus camera of 13.6 to 31.8 mm: pose tags are archived independently of the probe flag

recomputed_with_the_camera_lever.method: body pitch is genuinely measured, so the rocking term was recomputed against the camera optical centre height of 1.0416 m rather than the body origin
recomputed_with_the_camera_lever.reading: Body pitch changes by at most 3 mrad over these intervals, so even with the camera's larger lever it accounts for under 3.2 mm of a 13 to 32 mm gap. Mount flex is the obvious remaining candidate and was not measured. Tyre slip is also not excluded.

retraction_2026_09_16.consequence_for_step_1: The trigger was added so that an alert would leave the evidence explaining it. It did not: the fields that evidence depends on sit behind a flag the capture runs never set. The dumps exist and the window is correct, but the three quantities that would discriminate are absent.
retraction_2026_09_16.fix_for_the_next_series: enable probe_contact_kinematics for the full-area runs, not only the startup probes, and check its cost first: it also turns on EnableVelocityChecks for the wheel links (gz_linescan.cpp:289), which is presumably why it is opt-in.

alert_cause_closed_2026_09_16.cause: All thirteen alerts are the body pitch reference effect measured at the camera's lever. Pitch about the contact plane displaces every point on the vehicle horizontally by its own height times the pitch change. The encoder measures ground travel; the alert compares it against the camera optical centre, which is the point with the longest lever.
alert_cause_closed_2026_09_16.user_identified_it: The explanation is the user's: braking and acceleration pitch changes the camera's view. My three earlier readings -- re-imaged ground, an imaging-chain projection or timing fault, and stale pose tags across a hold boundary -- were each wrong and are withdrawn.

evidence.one_to_one: encoder minus camera against camera height times pitch change over the thirteen intervals: correlation 0.9528, slope 0.992
evidence.lever_ratio_test: sign-free and magnitude-free: (encoder-body)/(body-camera) should equal h_body/(h_camera-h_body) = 1.593 for pure pitch about the contact plane. Eleven of thirteen fall within 0.35 of it.
evidence.worked_example: the pause-resume alert in run 1, ratio 0.3917. Pitch change -12.269 mrad over 61 lines. Ground footprint at height 0 moves 22.30 mm, matching the encoder exactly. base_link at 0.648 m moves 22.30 - 7.95 = 14.35 mm, and 0.648*12.269 mrad = 7.95 mm exactly. The camera centre at 1.0416 m moves 9.52 predicted against 8.70 observed.
evidence.pixels_agree: adjacent-row difference over the flagged 61 rows is 9.305 against a block median of 8.644, i.e. normal spacing. That is only consistent with the ground footprint having tracked the encoder, and it is what falsified the re-imaging reading.
evidence.pause_drift_explained: the camera centre moves back 27.0 mm during the 3.66 s pause. Braking pitches the nose down about 1.44 deg; relaxing to level on stopping retracts the camera by 1.0416 m * 25 mrad = 26 mm.

consequence_for_the_rule.corrected_ratio: comparing the encoder against the ground footprint, camera centre plus height times pitch, puts all thirteen between 0.9571 and 0.9988
consequence_for_the_rule.this_is_not_relaxing_the_threshold: 0.95 is unchanged. The metric was comparing ground travel against a point a metre above the ground on a pitching body, so it was measuring the wrong point. Real sliding would still be caught, because pitch cannot explain it.
consequence_for_the_rule.recommended: keep the floor at 0.95 and correct the reference point in tools/audit_scan_slip.py and in the plugin's online check, using the body pitch already recorded in every sample

what_this_does_not_settle: contact tangential velocity was still never measured, so sliding is not independently excluded; it is simply no longer needed to explain these thirteen
the residual 0.5 to 4.9 mm after the pitch term is unattributed; mount flex is the obvious candidate and remains unmeasured
whether the same correction accounts for alerts on the 3 mm road, where the startup probes found a larger body-level gap
